subsystems.name: Matrix compute array
subsystems.role: does the bulk of neural-network maths — multiplying and accumulating large blocks of numbers.

subsystems.name: On-chip memory
subsystems.role: keeps data close to the compute units so they are not starved.
parts: memory controller for LPDDR or HBM

subsystems.name: Dataflow controller
subsystems.role: schedules how tensors are tiled, fed and pipelined through the array.

subsystems.name: Low-precision arithmetic units
subsystems.role: support the reduced number formats that make on-device inference efficient.

subsystems.name: Host and system interface
subsystems.role: connects the NPU to the CPU, GPU and shared memory of the device.
parts: PCIe or proprietary link for discrete NPUs

subsystems.name: Software stack
subsystems.role: turns a trained model into commands the NPU can execute.
parts: APIs such as ONNX, Core ML or DirectML

buildSteps.title: Design the dataflow
buildSteps.detail: Architects choose how data moves through the chip — how many multiply-accumulate units, what precision, how much on-chip memory — by simulating common neural-network layers.

buildSteps.title: Write and verify the RTL
buildSteps.detail: The design is described in a hardware description language, then verified against software models to catch functional bugs before fabrication.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise and place-and-route
buildSteps.detail: Tools convert the RTL into a transistor-level layout, placing logic cells and routing wires while meeting timing and power targets.

buildSteps.title: Tape out
buildSteps.detail: The finished layout becomes a set of photomasks sent to a semiconductor foundry.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the die
buildSteps.detail: The foundry builds the NPU block alongside CPU, GPU and memory controllers on a silicon wafer using an advanced CMOS process, layer by layer.

buildSteps.title: Package and test
buildSteps.detail: Wafers are diced, good dies are packaged, and each part is tested for speed, power and defects.

buildSteps.title: Enable the software
buildSteps.detail: Compilers, kernel libraries and drivers are written so that popular model formats can run on the new hardware.

prerequisites.why: dense, low-power logic is what allows billions of operations per second in a phone or laptop.
reducing weights and activations to 8 or 4 bits cuts memory traffic and power with little loss of accuracy.
neural networks are memory-bound; fast SRAM and LPDDR/HBM keep the compute units fed.
mapping a model efficiently across CPU, GPU and NPU is still hard and often vendor-specific.
ONNX and similar formats let developers target many NPUs without rewriting models.

pathway.milestone: NPUs in phones and PCs delivering tens of TOPS for local speech, image and language tasks.
pathway.unlocks: private, low-latency AI that works offline.

pathway.milestone: Chiplet-based NPUs and unified memory architectures that scale to hundreds of TOPS.

pathway.unlocks: models that adapt to a user without sending data to the cloud.

pathway.milestone: Always-on, microwatt NPUs for sensors and wearables.
pathway.unlocks: continuous AI in tiny battery-powered devices.
